evidence: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:144-149: the catch block isn't empty. It adds each exception to a CopyOnWriteArrayList, and line 159 runs assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()). If that assertion fails, the Hamcrest mismatch message prints the list, so each exception's class and message are reported. The only thing lost is the stack trace. Logging the exception (or attaching it as a suppressed exception on failure) would make debugging easier, but the reviewer overstates the problem when calling it a swallowed exception. There is also a stray blank line at 147.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:121,129,152: the local variable is spelled 'groupUuuids' (three u's), while the lambda variables beside it use 'groupUuid' (lines 128, 152). It is an obvious typo. Renaming it to 'groupUuids' is a trivial, behavior-neutral change. Low priority.

server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/GroupModel.java:293-298: the Javadoc says getSubGroupsCount() 'Never returns null', and model/infinispan/.../cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java:274-275 now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null (the group was deleted concurrently). So the contract claim is technically true. However, the only caller, services/.../utils/GroupUtils.java:90, passes the value to GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(Long) (core/.../idm/GroupRepresentation.java:94), which accepts a nullable Long. Nothing unboxes it, so there is no NPE risk. Returning 0L would quietly misreport a deleted group as having no subgroups, while null correctly means 'unknown'. The better fix is to update the Javadoc to allow null (or document the concurrent-delete case) rather than switch to 0L.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:140-159: the reader thread is started and never joined. Line 157 sets deletedAll and line 159 asserts right away, so an exception from a read still in flight can be added after the assertion has run and go unnoticed. The thread can also outlive the test. Joining the thread before the assertion is a real, cheap improvement. In practice the reader does start, because it overlaps with 100 synchronous HTTP DELETE calls (lines 152-155). That makes the CountDownLatch, the read counter and the 'multiple reads' assertion nice-to-have hardening against the test passing without exercising anything, not fixes for a test that is broken.
